svg.title: How vision picks frames
svg.desc: A strip of sixteen keyframes taken off a video's timeline, one every few seconds. Five never become candidates: a near-copy, a cross-fade, a blank frame, and two inside a sponsor span. Three routes can pick from the rest, and the first that is set up does. One, with a decision key: a decision model scores each picture, plus a little when it shows what is being said; talking heads fall under the 0.30 line, two neighbouring frames of the same item keep one, and a frame too close to a pick is skipped. Two, otherwise, with timed speech: embeddings match each frame to the keywords, sentences, and paragraphs said around it. Three, otherwise: the frame nearest the middle of each equal time slot, whatever it shows. The picks land on collage pages, three rows of two by default, in time order, each with its timestamp.

g.text: scores each picture, plus a little for showing what is said
match each frame to what is said around it, at three scales
take the frame nearest the middle of each equal slot, whatever it shows
plus: it shows what is said
